narrative:
The model estimates a 70% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your professional background.

Your total years of experience across all roles was the strongest factor pushing the prediction toward leaving. With 6-10 years overall, you sit in a mid-range group where many employees start considering new opportunities, unlike the majority of those predicted to stay who have only 1-5 years of total experience. Similarly, the time you have spent in your current organization (1-5 years) was the second most influential factor and also increased the likelihood of departure. Employees predicted to stay tend to have either much shorter or notably longer tenures here, suggesting that this intermediate period often coincides with restlessness or external prospects.

The third most important element actually worked in your favor: you have not received other job offers while at this company. This lack of external opportunities pulled the prediction back toward staying. However, it was not enough to outweigh the combined influence of your experience levels.

The organization should consider discussing your career goals openly with you and exploring ways to increase your sense of stability and growth potential here. You may want to reflect on what would make staying more appealing before deciding on your next steps. (218 words)
